what_the_class_is: The 3D delay as a whole: the three-tap delay's line, taps, levels, loop and damping, on the 0 - 500 ladder, the centre tap to both outputs and the side taps to their own, then the balance, level and tone stages.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at 32 kHz with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A delay is a circular buffer addressed by a sample count, so a time is a whole number of samples and a tap is one more read of the same buffer; three or four taps cost three or four reads and no more memory.

A loop takes a read of the buffer, scales it and adds it to what is written, and damping in it is the cheapest pole there is -- one multiply and one state -- because it only has to take the top off the repeats.
Whether the value fed back is the read of this sample or of the last one is a question of how the program is scheduled, and either costs the same.
Times, rates, levels and corners are tables indexed by the byte, as the classes that read them closed on; a whole-type model borrows those tables rather than fitting its own.
era.would_be_wrong_if: The repeats of a held or struck note came back at spacings other than the ladder entry (or the entry and a sample) at settings nothing here was built on, or their level fell per repeat by other than the printed feedback times the damping pole.

candidates.reading: The loop is fed from the centre tap before its level. The loop returns straight off the line at the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: With Dly Lev C at 0 the side taps keep reading recirculated copies spaced at the centre time, and a centre time of 0 has no order to be drawn in.

candidates.reading: The loop is fed from the centre tap before its level. The loop returns through a second read of the line one sample past the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: With Dly Lev C at 0 the side taps keep reading recirculated copies, each repeat a sample later than the ladder puts it.

candidates.reading: The loop is fed from the centre tap after its level. The loop returns straight off the line at the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: With Dly Lev C at 0 the loop is cut and nothing repeats, and a centre time of 0 has no order to be drawn in.

candidates.reading: The loop is fed from the centre tap after its level. The loop returns through a second read of the line one sample past the ladder entry.
candidates.predicts: With Dly Lev C at 0 the loop is cut and nothing repeats; otherwise each repeat is a sample later than the ladder puts it.

what_no_candidate_here_predicts: The placement the Out byte renders for speakers or phones. No claim reads it on this type, and the placement claim says there is no byte here to move an image with, so the byte is held at its power-on Speaker and the side taps go straight to their own outputs.
How the inputs are summed onto the line: half of each here; no reading fixed it.

Whether a tap level is the output level's stored curve: the level claim is carried to these bytes unmeasured. The power-on levels 40, 64 and 64 sit where the curve and the byte over 127 part by up to two decibels, so the takes at those levels bear on it.
Anything at the addresses the page does not print: no node reads them, so every candidate renders them as the power-on state.
Whether the damping claim, closed on the stereo delay and checked on the mod delay, reaches this type's HF Damp byte: it is carried here unmeasured, one pole on the line's input inside the loop.
